newsitem.title: CHINA: HK blue-chip Hang Seng Index gets new reddish tint.
newsitem.headline: HK blue-chip Hang Seng Index gets new reddish tint.

text.p: Only weeks after Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule, its blue chip Hang Seng Index has taken on a new reddish tint with a long-awaited reshuffle that added two China play stocks to the benchmark barometer.

HSI Services Ltd, the compiler of the 33-company Hang Seng Index, said on Wednesday that red chip China Resources Enterprise Ltd and Cheung Kong Infrastructure Holdings Ltd would join the index on July 31.
Red chips are mainland-backed Hong Kong-based companies.
An index reshuffle had been widely expected following a surge in the market capitalisation of red chip stocks this year.
China Resources, also a component of the newly created red chip Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporations Index, had been considered a leading candidate for blue-chip status.
Analysts had expected a switch soon after Hong Kong's change in sovereignty. The former British colony became a Special Administrative Region of China on July 1.

"The fact that infrastructure and red chips are two major groups that were under-represented previously and these are two of the larger companies in those particular sectors, it was important that they were included," said Andrew Fernow, director of research at Vickers Ballas.
China Resources and Cheung Kong Infrastructure replace Oriental Press Group Ltd and Johnson Electric Holdings Ltd in the Hang Seng Index.
"The market capitalisation of the Hang Seng Index after the replacements is expected to account for 70 percent of total market capitalisation," HSI Services spokesman Tony Chiu said.
He said the Hang Seng Index accounted for about 68-69 percent of total market capitalisation at the end of June.

Both China Resources and Cheung Kong Infrastructure each have market capitalisations of more than HK$50 billion, said Howard Gorges, vice chairman at South China Holdings. "They are bigger than quite a lot of the existing blue chips," he said.
Analysts said trading conglomerate China Resources, a red chip favourite, brought a much-needed China element to the index.
Cheung Kong Infrastructure is also considered a China play, with its new infrastructure projects focused on China.

"All of its new projects are coming out of China and it is concentrating on China infrastructure development," said Fernow. "Right now it has considerable assets in Hong Kong but in the future, that will shift into China," he said.

Both stocks are expected to gain on Thursday. "I think this will be very important for Cheung Kong Infrastructure in terms of targeting exposure by institutional investors. China Resources was already quite actively traded," said Fernow.
Gorges said the Hang Seng Index still needed more China exposure, and he expected another reshuffle over the coming year.
HSI Services reviews the Hang Seng Index quarterly. The last index reshuffle was announced in July 1996.
"There will likely be more changes coming as these red chips emerge," said Gorges. "It does give the index more China focus, but it is still not substantially China focused."
HSI Services also said it would make changes to its Hang Seng MidCap 50 Index on July 31, adding Oriental Press Group, Johnson Electric, Goldlion Holdings Ltd and Henderson China Holdings Ltd.

HSI Services said it would remove China Resources, Pudong Development Holdings Ltd, Sing Tao Holdings Ltd and Stelux Holdings International Ltd from the Hang Seng MidCap 50 Index. It said the index is expected to account for about nine percent of total market capitalisation.
